import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## Symptom

A background operator (`bin/hono-host.ts` with `PAPERCUSP_BACKGROUND_WORKERS=1`) grows
retained RSS **~1-9 GB/min** with no plateau until the memory-watchdog recycles it
(12-32 GB). Worst on the **desktop's `:3270`** operator (getting hammered) at **~9 GB/min →
hits the 32 GB limit in ~4 min → recycle loop**, which blanks the desktop
("Papercusp lost its operator process") and repeatedly interrupts **git-sync** (the recycle
kills the in-flight commit → the fleet-wide "git-sync STALLED" broadcasts). Also shows as
`[event-loop-lag] high loop delay — CPU-bound on the main thread` (p50 > 1500 ms).

## Root cause (the one the prior hunt missed)

The prior leak hunt (`bg-host-freeze-eventloop-stall-2026-06-30` P-005 / WI-1088/1089)
chased the **Hypercore/Corestore P2P layer** and fixed a real Hyperswarm connection-listener
leak — but the DOMINANT driver was elsewhere and stayed live.

A **sampling heap profiler** (see the tool below) showed **~84-88% of all allocation** was
`path.join`, called from **`claude-sessions.ts` `claudeProjectsRoots()` / `findSessionTranscript()`** —
a recursive filesystem sweep:

- `claudeProjectsRoots()` `readdir`s the isolation base `~/.papercusp/session-claude/` — **12k+
  per-owner dirs on a long-lived box** — and builds a `path.join` per owner.
- `findSessionTranscript(sessionId)` **only cached POSITIVE resolutions**. Any unresolvable id
  (a dead/ephemeral session, or a transcript not yet written) fell through to the **full sweep of
  every root** — and re-ran it on **every call** (no negative cache).
- The hot caller: **`compaction-usage.ts`'s watchdog** polls `estimateContextTokensForOwner`
  on a cadence for **many owners**, calling `findSessionTranscript(sessionId)` **with no `owner`
  hint** — so each miss re-swept all 12k+ dirs.

Why it manifests as *retained* RSS, not just churn: `NODE_OPTIONS` carries
`--max-old-space-size=131072` (128 GB), which defeats V8's heap-limit-paced GC, and the
watchdog's proactive GC only fires **every 2 min at 60% of the limit**. So a ~100s-of-MB/s
transient-allocation firehose accumulates uncollected garbage up to the recycle ceiling before
GC catches up — a churn leak that reads as a retention leak.

## Fix

Three bounds in `claude-sessions.ts` + an owner hint in the caller:

1. **Negative-resolution TTL cache** (`transcriptMissCache`, 30 s) — an id known-missing
   short-circuits the whole sweep. Short TTL so a not-yet-written transcript re-resolves once it
   appears; lightly pruned so unique ids can't grow it unbounded.
2. **Roots TTL cache** (`defaultProjectsRootsCached`, 15 s) — the 12k-dir isolation-base readdir
   runs ~once per window, not per lookup. Only the default-args hot path is cached; explicit-roots
   callers (tests / targeted scans) bypass.
3. **`__resetClaudeSessionCaches()`** test seam.
4. **`compaction-usage.ts` passes the `owner` hint** → `findSessionTranscript`'s fast path (one
   owner-root readdir), not the full sweep.

## Verification (live, on a fresh patched operator)

- Allocation: **428 MB → 8.2 MB per 20 s (~52×)**; `path.join`/`claudeProjectsRoots` gone from
  the top allocators.
- RSS **reclaimed** 12.7 → 8.25 GB mid-window (GC catches up now) and growth dropped
  **~9 → ~0.9 GB/min (~10×)** — sawtoothing (healthy), not the monotonic climb to 32 GB.
- 24 unit tests pass, incl. 3 new recurrence guards in `claude-sessions-cache.test.ts`.

## The tool: `scripts/leak-sample.mjs`

<Aside type="tip" title="Sampling profiler beats a full heap snapshot for a FAST leak">
For a multi-GB/min leak, a full `.heapsnapshot` is huge + slow and only shows RETENTION.
The V8 **sampling heap profiler** (`HeapProfiler.startSampling`) is low-overhead, tiny output,
and names the exact **allocating call stack** — which is what you want when the leak is
allocation-churn. `scripts/leak-sample.mjs <pid> [ms]` sends `SIGUSR1` to open the target's
inspector, samples for the window, and prints the top allocation sites by bytes.
</Aside>

## Remaining baseline (~0.9 GB/min — follow-ups, prior WI-1089 territory)

With the fs-sweep gone, the residual slow growth is the correctness-sensitive P2P internals a
static-analysis subagent flagged (do NOT rush — evicting merge/replication state can corrupt reads):

- **Corestore replication-stream teardown** on unclean peer disconnect (`swarm.ts:737`
  `store.replicate(socket)` — the in-process default path never got the `pipeWithMutualTeardown`
  fix that only landed on the dark sidecar path). Dangling Protomux muxer + per-core send/recv
  buffers × ~25 stores per churned peer.
- **`read-merge.ts` `MergeCursor.winners` Map** — unbounded per distinct immutable federated
  op-key × 25 harnesses; wiped only on a log-set change / `forceReFold`.
- **`stall-waker.ts` `lastWokeAt`/`lastUnwedgeAt`/`wakeCount`** — never pruned per ephemeral owner
  (small; MB-over-days).
